CSCO.rationale: Cisco's stock has surged +51.9% in one quarter to $118.64, pushing the P/E to 42.7x — the highest in the 365-day window (range 25.8–43.3) and nearly double the ~26x level from a year ago. This extreme re-rating has occurred despite deteriorating fundamentals: operating cash flow collapsed -43.3% QoQ and -18.7% YoY in the latest quarter, adjusted gross margin compressed to 66.0% from 68.6% due to memory costs and tariff headwinds (described as persistent, not transitory), and security revenue was flat YoY at ~$2B, exposing the weakest part of the portfolio. RPO growth decelerated to 5% YoY, lagging the 10% total revenue growth, indicating the company is not converting the AI hardware cycle into durable recurring revenue. The P/B of 9.9x is also at the top of its range (5.5–10.1). While revenue and EPS growth are solid (YoY revenue +9.7%, EPS +31.1%), the valuation now prices in far more than the fundamentals justify. Key risks include intensifying competition from Arista and Nvidia in AI networking, margin pressure from tariffs and memory costs, and the faltering software transition. The stock appears to be trading on AI hype rather than fundamental improvement, creating significant downside risk to the stretched multiple.
